subject: Logic
title: The Chinese Room
description: A quick, practical guide to The Chinese Room.

hook.text: A person in a room follows rules to answer Chinese questions perfectly—without understanding a word of Chinese.

buildup.text: John Searle designed this in 1980 to argue that computers manipulate symbols without understanding meaning.

discovery.text: The room passes every language test—but nobody inside understands Chinese. Simulation isn't comprehension.

twist.text: AI researchers objected: maybe the room as a whole understands, even if the person inside doesn't.

climax.text: The debate continues. Can any system built on rules alone ever truly understand—or just convincingly pretend?

punchline.text: Perfect answers without understanding a word.

quiz.question: What does the Chinese Room argument challenge?
options: Whether computers can truly understand meaning
